step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core visual entities from the whiteboard and video description: Client (UserConsumerDeveloper), AppGate Controller (EC2), SSO (IAM), IAM (IAM), Route 53 (Route53), AppGate Gateway (EC2), AutoScaling (AutoScaling), and VPC (VPC).
2. Structured user flows based on diagram arrows and audio explanation:
   - Flow 0: Client sends Single Packet Authorization (SPA) to EC2 APPGATE controller, which authenticates user via SSO and checks permissions via IAM, returning an entitlement token back to Client.
   - Flow 1: Client resolves target host names using Route 53 DNS.
   - Flow 2: Client establishes an encrypted connection through the AppGate Gateway to access target resources in the VPC.
3. Formatted nodes and edges cleanly following all schema and vocabulary constraints.

graph.notes: AppGate SDP (Software Defined Perimeter) architecture on AWS, using Single Packet Authorization (SPA), identity integration (SSO/IAM), and dynamic AppGate Gateways for zero trust client access to VPC resources.

edges.notes: Client sends SPA (Single Packet Authorization) request to the AppGate Controller.
AppGate Controller authenticates user identity via SSO identity provider.
AppGate Controller evaluates permissions and roles via AWS IAM.
AppGate Controller returns entitlement token and routing configuration back to Client.
Client performs DNS host resolution via Route 53.
Client connects via secure parallel encrypted tunnel to AppGate Gateway.
AppGate Gateway routes authorized traffic to target host resources inside the VPC.
